clue.text: Nautical course — a difficult one?

definitions.meaning: the ship's biscuit served to sailors as their staple dish, a course of a meal at sea
a sailing tack that is hard going, a tough leg on the water

explanation.surface: A sailing route is described, with the speaker wondering whether it will be a tough one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a route on the water, but the first sense is a course of a meal: the dry biscuit eaten by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' rations long centred on a dry, hard biscuit, while a tack is also a leg sailed against the wind.

clue.text: Jack appears to offend with article featuring drink.

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, as is an AB, an able seaman
to sin is to offend
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A man named Jack seems to offend by writing an article about drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and AB are both crossword words for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A green aniseed-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood is a strong alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Very sad delay in desert island programme?

definitions.meaning: read as '...', a record played late on Desert Island Discs, the BBC radio show where guests choose music

explanation.surface: A listener is upset at a delay to a radio show about a desert island.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert Island Discs is a long-running BBC radio programme; the answer split as DISC ON SO LATE gives the delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond comfort in grief is extremely unhappy, a synonym.

clue.text: Chance for sleuths to get in a bit of money

indicators.note: to get in means the sleuths go inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives see an opportunity to get hold of some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in' puts CID inside CENT, after A. CID is the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens by luck rather than design is a synonym for chance.

clue.text: County doctor screened

definitions.meaning: a county of Ireland, in Leinster
Dr ..., the hero of a 1960s television drama shown on screen

explanation.surface: A county medic is examined or shielded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screened' looks like medically tested; it means shown on television, where Dr Kildare was a popular series.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish county shares its name with the fictional doctor of a hit television drama.

clue.text: The main issue of the time

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the chief topic of the moment is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main issue' reads as the chief topic; it is the sea's son.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of the year, such as summer, is a stretch of time.

clue.text: Lot of money in building

definitions.meaning: a large imposing building, a stately home

explanation.surface: A great deal of cash is tied up in property.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is informally a heap of money, and a grand mansion is also called by the same word for a heap.

clue.text: Top headline for the English in 1984

parts.note: a headline item is news
a peak is the top

explanation.surface: A leading news story for the English in the year 1984.
explanation.walkthrough: 1984 is Orwell's novel, whose invented official language replaces English.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's novel imagines a pared-down official language replacing standard speech in Oceania.

clue.text: Building Elsie and Ida regard as perfect

indicators.note: the two names are built up into a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Two women, Elsie and Ida, admire a building as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like the thing being admired, but it signals the anagram of ELSIE and IDA.
explanation.definitionFit: To think of something as flawless or ideal is a plain synonym.

clue.text: One relative some say was worshipped

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
sis is a familiar word for sister, as some people say it

explanation.surface: A relative of the speaker, some claim, was once revered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some say' marks SIS as the informal way people say sister; the definition is cryptic, naming the Egyptian goddess as one who was worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Egyptian goddess, wife of Osiris, received worship across the Nile world.

clue.text: Second in last scene on the world stage

definitions.text: Second in last scene on the world stage

parts.words: Second in last scene on the world stage
parts.note: a quotation from As You Like It: in the speech 'All the world's a stage', the last scene of life is the second spell of infant behaviour

explanation.surface: An actor appears second in the final scene of a worldwide performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's Seven Ages of Man speech ends with old age as 'second childishness and mere oblivion'; 'Second' reads as a position but is part of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare describes old age as a return to infancy, the second time a person behaves like an infant.

clue.text: Like contents of the widow's cruse all the same

definitions.text: Like contents of the widow's cruse
definitions.meaning: in the Bible (1 Kings 17) the widow's jar of oil never ran down, never getting smaller

explanation.surface: Someone compares the contents of a widow's jar, saying it is unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: The widow's cruse in the Book of Kings held oil that never diminished: split, the answer reads 'never the less'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for 'however' or 'in spite of that' is also the phrase for never being diminished.

clue.text: Position of club director?

parts.note: the club is a golf club, and the person directing it at the ball takes up a set posture with the feet

explanation.surface: Someone asks what post the director of a sports club holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club director' looks like a committee role; it is a golfer aiming the club, and 'Position' is how they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's set posture before striking the ball is the standard term for how they stand.

clue.text: Renew agitation by Tree about star

indicators.note: about means the stirred letters go around the star word
agitation stirs the letters of Tree into a new order

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: An actor named Tree gets worked up about a star, wanting renewal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitation' turns TREE into RETE, and 'about' puts that round NOVA. Tree reads as the actor-manager Herbert Beerbohm Tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something to good condition is to make it new again, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Goes and makes other arrangements

definitions.meaning: as in '... to', turns or goes to something for help

explanation.surface: Someone leaves and changes their plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as RE-SORTS, sorting again.
explanation.definitionFit: One who has recourse to a remedy turns to it, and to re-sort things is to order them afresh.

clue.text: Witty retort about some key duplication

parts.note: re means about, concerning
part means some, a portion

indicators.note: duplication says the musical key letter appears twice

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A clever reply about copying some keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplication' doubles E, a musical key, giving EE.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-witted banter or a clever comeback is a synonym for a witty reply.

clue.text: He gives father a turn

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a trick is a turn, as a spell of duty or a stage act

explanation.surface: A man gives his dad a spin or a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name stands for a man, as the pronoun does.

clue.text: One missing from a working party sent inside

indicators.note: inside means the word sent is placed within the working party

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for communal work, as in a sewing bee

explanation.surface: Someone absent from a work group is sent in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts SENT within BEE, after A. A bee is a social gathering for shared work, such as a quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is away when expected is not present, so they are not there.

clue.text: Soldier appears to have no authority

parts.note: command means authority
O is nought, nothing, no

explanation.surface: A soldier seems to lack any authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no authority' reads as lacking power; the pieces are COMMAND and O, nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an elite raiding unit is a type of soldier.

clue.text: Girl is up river in bad trouble

indicators.note: in places the turned river within the scrambled letters
trouble stirs the letters of bad into a new order
is up means the river is read upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: the Nile is the river of Egypt

explanation.surface: A girl who has gone up the river is in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns NILE into ELIN, and 'trouble' turns BAD into BDA; ELIN goes in after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name stands for a girl.

clue.text: Introduction made before walk

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
an amble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: An opening speech was delivered before a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening statement that leads into a document or speech is a synonym for an introduction.

clue.text: Buffet head gets lift from cook

indicators.note: head means just the first letter of Buffet

parts.note: raise means lift

explanation.surface: A head waiter at the buffet gets a lift from the chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a meal; only its first letter is used. 'cook' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat slowly in a covered pot with a little liquid is a method of cooking.

clue.text: Plan to mechanise but not in a new form

indicators.note: but not means the letters of the following words are taken away from the longer word
new form says the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proposal to mechanise production, though not in an updated form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes I, N and A from MECHANISE, leaving MECHSE, which 'new form' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or systematic arrangement for doing something, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Sensible to include, woman student of St John's work

indicators.note: to include means the reasonable word holds the next pieces within it

parts.note: rational means sensible, reasonable
Eve is the first woman in Genesis
L is the learner plate on a car, for a student driver

explanation.surface: A sensible woman student is included in a project on St John's college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts EVEL inside RATIONAL. St John's work is the Book of Revelation, traditionally attributed to John.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective describing the Apocalypse, the last book of the Bible ascribed to the apostle John.

clue.text: Fault of singer, nothing less

indicators.note: less means the following nothing is taken away

parts.note: a voice is a singer, as in a choir's best voices
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A singer is blamed for a fault, nothing less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O from VOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral failing or weakness is a fault.

clue.text: Bird provides service in midweek

indicators.note: in means the service letters go inside the middle of week

parts.note: the middle two letters of week are E and E
RN is the Royal Navy, a fighting service

explanation.surface: A bird puts on a show in the middle of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midweek' gives the middle letters of 'week'; the Royal Navy (RN) is one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a crossword favourite among birds of prey.

clue.text: Shut in by old scene-shifter

indicators.note: a scene-shifter moves things around, so it signals that the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was locked in by an elderly stagehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scene-shifter' reads as a theatre stagehand; 'shifter' is the anagram signal working on OLD SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fenced or walled around is confined within, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Declares no-one returned dislike

parts.note: avers means asserts or declares

indicators.note: returned means the letters for no and one are read backwards

parts.note: no gives NO and one is I

explanation.surface: Someone says that nobody came back, showing distaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-one' looks like nobody, but splits into NO and I (one), which 'returned' turns into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling of distaste or antipathy is a synonym for dislike.
